## Introduction

This is a demonstration manuscript. It is a normal Quarto document
(`manuscript.qmd`) that cites the library's shared bibliography, so a citation
like @ingram2024 resolves against `.lctrn/references.bib` — the one bib
generated from the whole paper pile, not a per-project copy.

The question this stub sets up: mandatory climate disclosure changes what firms
publish, but does it change what investors learn? @ingram2024 finds a cost of
capital effect that appears only where the disclosure is assured, while
@vasquez2023 shows that a large share of mandated climate risk language is
recycled boilerplate. Read together they suggest that the binding constraint is
credibility rather than volume.

## What to try here

1. **Open a paper.** Double-click a row in Papers. The PDF opens in the reader
   with a notes pane beside it; notes are saved as markdown under `notes/`.
2. **Cite one.** Type `@` in this editor to pull up citekey completion from the
   library.
3. **Render it.** Render to PDF or HTML — this needs Quarto installed.
4. **Hand it to Claude.** Open the terminal below and ask for something concrete,
   e.g. *"tighten the introduction and make sure every claim cites a paper in the
   bibliography"*. Claude Code runs in this folder and edits the same files you
   are looking at.
5. **Review what changed.** Every turn is snapshotted, so the review panel shows
   what Claude touched, grouped by the prompt that caused it, with keep or revert
   per file.

## Notes

The three papers in this library are fictional, generated to give the demo
something with a real text layer to search. Replace them with your own PDFs —
drop them into `sources/` and the watcher will register them.
